heading: Error handlers
body: ErrorHandler marks a class that answers typed errors for every controller of its language. Put it in server/controllers/NameErrorHandler.ext. HandlesError marks one of its instance methods and takes no argument. The declared type of the first parameter is the error that the method handles. JavaScript declares that type with JSDoc, such as @param {OrderNotFound} error. An optional second parameter receives the request in the language's own type, such as a Fetch Request or HttpExchange. PHP handlers take no second parameter and read the superglobals. ResponseStatus on that method sets an error status from 400 to 599; the default is 500. An error type is a normal error class or type in server/errors/Type.ext, with no annotation. The nearest type wins, so a subclass handler runs before a base class handler. Two methods that handle the same error type are refused, also when they are in different handler classes. An error that no method handles keeps the fixed 500 answer, and so does an error that a handler throws itself: handling never runs again on its own error. OPTIONS and /api.json list the error types of each route with their status and answer shape. Go matches with errors.As. Rust matches the error type of the controller method's Result. Spring's ControllerAdvice and ExceptionHandler and NestJS's ExceptionFilter and UseFilters are refused; use ErrorHandler and HandlesError. See [error handlers](/docs/error-handlers) for an example in every Yon language.
